routes.description: Infer a supernatural, intelligent, and moral creator from features of reality, then connect that creator specifically to the biblical God through Jesus.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if its causal, design, and moral inferences establish the relevant divine attributes and the Jesus evidence supplies the biblical identification.

motionBridge.description: The inferred creator must be identified with the God of the Bible rather than only an unspecified supernatural cause.

centralBridges.description: The universe's existence and beginning must require a cause beyond physical matter.
Fine-tuning and complex functional organization must warrant an inference to intelligence.
Objective moral obligations must require a personal moral source beyond naturalistic preference.
The historical case concerning Jesus must support resurrection and divine identity.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Human fallibility must remain compatible with knowledge of burden-relevant foundational truths.
Suffering must be compatible with divine goodness through a coherent redemptive or ultimate account.

routes.description: Withhold the biblical-theist conclusion by showing that natural explanations, evidential limits, religious diversity, and suffering undercut its necessary inferences.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the affirmative evidence does not discriminate the biblical God from natural alternatives, uncertainty, rival religions, or unsupported supernatural claims.

motionBridge.description: The total evidence must fail to justify the existence and specifically biblical identity asserted in the motion.

centralBridges.description: Confidence in supernatural claims must remain proportioned to testable and publicly available support.
Causation, biological complexity, morality, and apparent design must admit nondivine explanations or remain unresolved.
Biblical revelation and resurrection claims must withstand comparison with informed disagreement and rival traditions.
Apparently gratuitous innocent suffering must be reconciled with the claimed omnipotent and benevolent God.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Finite human access to objective truth must warrant intellectual humility and revisability.
Methodological naturalism must provide a workable standard for detecting causal interaction and comparing explanations.

sections.title: Knowledge and Evidential Standards
sections.rationale: The permissible degree of certainty and the testability of supernatural claims govern how every substantive inference in the debate can bear the motion-level burden.

sections.title: Cosmic Causation
sections.rationale: The first-cause inference is an independent path from the universe to a nonphysical creator, while objections contest whether the regress identifies any God.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning and Biological Design
sections.rationale: The design dispute determines whether cosmic parameters and functional biological organization supply evidence of intelligence or remain explicable without a supernatural designer.

sections.title: Moral Objectivity and Natural Origins
sections.rationale: The grounding of objective moral standards bears on whether reality requires a personal moral God or whether morality can arise and function within naturalism.

sections.title: Jesus, Resurrection, and Religious Diversity
sections.rationale: This issue supplies the required bridge from generic theism to the biblical God and tests that identification against resurrection scrutiny and competing religious claims.

sections.title: Suffering and Divine Goodness
sections.rationale: The compatibility of innocent suffering with omnipotent benevolence bears directly on the asserted biblical God's attributes and on possible redemptive or afterlife explanations.
